prompt: Explain how an atom produces an emission spectrum.
markscheme: Electrons are excited to higher energy levels (by heat or electricity) **(A1)**; when they return to lower levels, they emit photons whose energy equals the difference between the levels, giving lines of specific frequencies **(R1)**

prompt: Why do the lines in the hydrogen emission spectrum get closer together at higher frequency?
options: Electrons move faster in higher levels
Energy levels get closer together at higher energies
Photons of high frequency travel more slowly
markscheme: **C.** The energy levels themselves converge as $n$ increases, so transitions from successive high levels differ less and less in energy.

concept: Electrons in a main energy level
prompt: What is the maximum number of electrons in the third main energy level ($n=3$)?
markscheme: **C.** $2n^{2}=18$: one 3s, three 3p and five 3d orbitals, each holding two electrons.

prompt: Write the full electron configurations of **(a)** Fe, **(b)** Fe³⁺, **(c)** Cr and **(d)** Cu.
markscheme:
**(a)** $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}3d^{6}4s^{2}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}3d^{5}$ — 4s electrons are removed before 3d **(A1)**

**(c)** $[\text{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$ **(A1)** **(d)** $[\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^{1}$ **(A1)** — half-filled and filled d sublevels are especially stable.

prompt: Draw (describe) the orbital diagram for the valence electrons of nitrogen and state the rule that determines how the 2p electrons are arranged.
markscheme:
2s: one box with two electrons of opposite spin; 2p: three boxes each with one electron, all with parallel spins **(A1)**

Hund's rule: electrons occupy orbitals of equal energy singly before pairing, minimising repulsion **(A1)**

concept: Ionisation energy from the convergence limit
prompt: The convergence limit of the hydrogen Lyman series is at $3.29\times10^{15}$ Hz. Calculate the first ionisation energy of hydrogen in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. ($h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J s, $N_A=6.02\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$)
markscheme:
At the convergence limit the electron moves from $n=1$ to $n=\infty$ (removed) **(R1)**

$E=hf=2.18\times10^{-18}$ J per atom **(A1)**; $\times N_A$, $\div1000$: $1.31\times10^{3}\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

prompt: The first five ionisation energies of element X (kJ mol⁻¹) are 738, 1451, 7733, 10540, 13630. Deduce the group of X and explain your answer.
markscheme: Group 2 **(A1)** — the large jump between the 2nd and 3rd IE shows that the third electron is removed from a lower main energy level, closer to the nucleus and less shielded, so X has two valence electrons **(R1)**
